correctness.rationale: For τ:A→B onto, the full zip shift on B^{Z<0}×A^{Z≥0} has precisely |τ^-1(y_{-1})| predecessors of y; the only unconstrained predecessor coordinate is x0. Every fixed point p^a consists of constant future letter a and constant past τ(a), giving c_d=d n_d where n_d counts transition fibres of cardinality d. Any homeomorphism conjugacy preserves fixed points and preimage cardinalities, hence each n_d. Conversely equal unordered fibre sizes yield bijections α:A→A′, β:B→B′ with τ′α=βτ; coordinatewise relabeling on two halves is an actual conjugacy. Thus conjugacy classes are indexed by partitions of N=|A| (or partitions with exactly M parts if |B|=M), and realizable polynomials have d|c_d and Σc_d=N. Periodic points have N^k possible length-k future words, ζ=(1−Nz)^−1; a two-sided A-shift factor onto Xτ and a one-sided A-shift factor from Xτ sandwich entropy at log N. Count formulas include all boundary cases N≥2 and positive fibre sizes.
residual_risks: Finite independent checks do not prove the all-parameter claims; analytic arguments or exhaustive certificates are required.

value.rationale: The partition-indexed *complete* topological conjugacy classification for a canonical natural family distinguishes systems invisible to entropy and ordinary zeta data. Fixed-point branching polynomials are a simple but mathematically motivated exact dynamical invariant, and no general theorem or paper-sized proof is required for a natural complete classification.
